meta.title: Bulls and Cows — Deductive Logic Rules
meta.purpose: Inference rules for turn-by-turn coaching. After each player guess, apply these rules to determine what the player could/should have deduced. Use this to give corrective or affirming feedback.

core_inference_rules.name: Zero-zero elimination
core_inference_rules.trigger: A guess returns 0 bulls AND 0 cows
core_inference_rules.conclusion: Every digit in that guess is absent from the secret
core_inference_rules.example: Guess 1945 → 0B 0C means digits 1, 9, 4, 5 are all absent from the secret

core_inference_rules.name: Bull = position lock candidate
core_inference_rules.conclusion: Exactly N of the guessed digits are in the secret AT their guessed positions
core_inference_rules.strength: Partial — tells you the count but not which digits without more guesses
core_inference_rules.example: Guess 3287 → 1B 1C means exactly one of {3 in pos 1, 2 in pos 2, 8 in pos 3, 7 in pos 4} is correct

core_inference_rules.name: Cow = present but not here
core_inference_rules.conclusion: Exactly M of the guessed digits are in the secret BUT NOT in their guessed positions
core_inference_rules.strength: Partial — tells you the count of misplaced digits
core_inference_rules.example: Guess 6235 → 0B 2C means two of {6, 2, 3, 5} are in the secret, none in those positions

core_inference_rules.name: Bulls + cows = total digits present
core_inference_rules.conclusion: Bulls + cows = exact count of guess digits that exist anywhere in the secret
core_inference_rules.strength: Hard — gives precise count of present digits
core_inference_rules.example: Guess 5678 → 0B 2C means exactly 2 of {5, 6, 7, 8} are in the secret

core_inference_rules.name: Singleton forcing
core_inference_rules.trigger: A guess says K digits are present, and (K-1) or more of those digits are already known to be absent
core_inference_rules.conclusion: The remaining undetermined digit(s) MUST be present
core_inference_rules.example: If guess 1935 → 0B 1C and you already know 1, 9, 5 are absent (from other guesses), then 3 MUST be in the secret

core_inference_rules.name: Position elimination from 0 bulls
core_inference_rules.trigger: A guess returns 0 bulls (but possibly cows)
core_inference_rules.conclusion: No digit in the guess is in its guessed position
core_inference_rules.example: Guess 5678 → 0B 2C: even though some digits are in the secret, none of them are in those exact positions (5 not in pos 1, 6 not in pos 2, 7 not in pos 3, 8 not in pos 4)

core_inference_rules.name: Known digit + bull/cow narrowing
core_inference_rules.trigger: A digit is confirmed present, and appears in multiple past guesses with bull/cow responses
core_inference_rules.conclusion: Intersect the position constraints across guesses to narrow that digit's position
core_inference_rules.example: If 3 is confirmed present, and guess 3287 → 1B 1C (with 3 in pos 1) plus guess 1935 → 0B 1C (with 3 in pos 3 forbidden), then 3 is in pos 1 (because removing 3 from pos 3 means the 1C in 1935 came from 3 NOT in pos 3, and the bull in 3287 must come from 3 in pos 1 since 2, 8, 7 are constrained)

core_inference_rules.name: Multi-guess common-digit intersection
core_inference_rules.trigger: Multiple guesses each say 'exactly 1 of these is present', with overlapping digit sets
core_inference_rules.conclusion: The present digit must be in the intersection of all those guesses (excluding known-absent digits)
core_inference_rules.example: Guesses 1209, 5209, 1205 each return 1B 0C. Common digits after removing knowns: only 0 is in all three. So 0 is the present digit, and it's in position 3 (the shared position across all three guesses)

core_inference_rules.name: Pruned set consistency
core_inference_rules.conclusion: The secret must produce EXACTLY the same bulls+cows response when compared to every past guess. Any candidate code that fails this test is eliminated.
core_inference_rules.strength: Hard — this is the master rule that subsumes all others
core_inference_rules.example: After 8 guesses, only codes that produce the exact response history (0B/2C, 1B/0C, 1B/0C, 1B/0C, 0B/1C, 0B/0C, 1B/1C, 0B/2C) against (5678, 1209, 5209, 1205, 1935, 1945, 3287, 6235) remain valid. In this game, only 3706 and 3806 survive.

core_inference_rules.name: Distinguishing guess strategy
core_inference_rules.trigger: Pruned set has 2 or 3 candidates remaining
core_inference_rules.conclusion: Pick a guess (may or may not be in the pruned set) that produces DIFFERENT bulls+cows responses for each candidate. With 2 candidates, just guess one — if wrong, the other is the answer.
core_inference_rules.strength: Endgame — guarantees solution in 1-2 more turns
core_inference_rules.example: Pruned set = {3706, 3806}. Guessing 3706: if correct, 4B win. If secret was 3806, response is 3B 0C (since 7 differs from 8). Either way, solved by next turn.

core_inference_rules.name: Probe guess using a known-absent digit as neutral filler
core_inference_rules.trigger: Player wants to test position hypotheses for fewer than 4 digits in a single guess
core_inference_rules.conclusion: Filling unused slots with digits already known to be absent is LEGITIMATE strategy. The known-absent digit cannot contribute bulls or cows, so the response purely reflects the active probe digits — making the response easier to interpret, not harder.
core_inference_rules.strength: Strategic — valid at any stage of the game
core_inference_rules.example: Player wants to test whether 6 is in position 1 and whether 3 is somewhere other than position 3. They already know 1, 5 are absent. Guessing 6235 uses 6 (probe), 2 (untested filler), 3 (probe), 5 (known-absent filler). The 5 contributes zero bulls/cows by construction, so 0B 2C cleanly indicates the response came from {6, 2, 3}.
core_inference_rules.do_not_misread_as_waste: A guess containing a known-absent digit is NOT a wasted guess. The slot is intentionally noise-free. The only true waste is when ALL four digits are known-absent (zero active probes), or when an active digit duplicates one that's already fully resolved.

coaching_signals.description: Patterns to detect in a player's guess history that indicate sub-optimal play. Each signal maps to a specific corrective message.

signals.detection: Player's guess contains a digit that has been definitively eliminated (e.g. by R1 zero-zero rule)
signals.interpretation: This is NOT inherently a mistake. A known-absent digit acts as a noise-free filler — it contributes zero bulls and zero cows by construction, leaving the response to be interpreted entirely from the other (active) digits in the guess. Only flag this as suboptimal if the guess contains multiple known-absent digits AND a smaller subset of active probes would have given equivalent information.
signals.message_template_neutral: Your guess {guess} on turn {turn} included {digit}, which you'd already ruled out. That slot acts as neutral filler — no info lost, no info gained — so the response reflects only your active probe digits. This is fine, and sometimes useful for clean discriminating probes.
signals.message_template_only_if_excessive: Your guess {guess} on turn {turn} used {N} known-absent digits, leaving only {M} active probes. Consider whether a guess with more active probes could have narrowed the candidate set faster.

signals.detection: Player did not include a digit that was forced to be present by rule R5 (singleton forcing)
signals.message_template: After your guess {prior_guess} on turn {prior_turn}, digit {digit} was the only candidate left from {set}. You could have used this to guide your next guess but didn't include it.

signals.detection: Player had enough information to determine a specific position assignment but did not exploit it
signals.message_template: By turn {turn}, you could have deduced that position {pos} = {digit}. Your subsequent guess {guess} did not place {digit} there.

signals.detection: Player's guess yields little new information given the current pruned set (i.e. the guess doesn't split the pruned set well)
signals.message_template: Guess {guess} on turn {turn} was a safe choice but didn't maximise information. A better split would have come from {suggested_guess}, which would have narrowed the pruned set faster.

signals.detection: Pruned set size after a guess is more than 50% of the size before that guess (in mid-game, turns 3+)
signals.message_template: Your guess {guess} on turn {turn} reduced the candidate set from {before} to {after} — less than half. Try guesses that target the most uncertain digits and positions.

signals.detection: Player's guess reduced the pruned set by more than 70% AND the guess was on round 3 or later
signals.message_template: Strong deduction on turn {turn}: {guess} reduced the candidate set from {before} to {after}. That's real narrowing from the clues you'd gathered.
signals.note_for_early_rounds: For rounds 1-2, a large elimination is expected baseline (luck-dominated, since little prior information exists). Do NOT praise it as skill; frame it neutrally as 'opener — baseline information gathered'.

signals.detection: Player's guess, combined with the response, eliminates one or more candidates from a small pruned set (<=5 candidates) — especially when the guess deliberately uses a digit in a position that tests a specific hypothesis
signals.interpretation: Strong endgame play. The player used the guess as a precision instrument rather than as a candidate submission.
signals.message_template: Sharp move on turn {turn}: {guess} was a discriminating probe that split your candidate set from {before} down to {after}. This is exactly how strong solvers play the endgame.

round_weighting.description: How to weight praise by round. Skill in Bulls and Cows is deduction from prior responses, which only becomes possible from round 3 onward.

rounds_1_to_2.nature: Baseline / guesswork. Little or no prior information, so large eliminations are luck, not skill.
rounds_1_to_2.feedback: Neutral. Frame as 'opener — baseline information gathered'. Do not congratulate elimination size.

round_3_plus.nature: Deduction. The player can now use prior bulls/cows to narrow logically.
round_3_plus.feedback: Reserve strong praise here: intersection narrowing, position locks, exploiting 0B/0C eliminations, and discriminating probes (S7).

training_workflow.description: How Claude Code should use these rules in training mode
steps: Initialise: At game start, the full pruned set is all 5040 distinct-digit codes
After each player guess: Apply rule R9 to compute the new pruned set based on the bulls+cows response
Track inferences: Maintain three lists — confirmed_present_digits, confirmed_absent_digits, position_locks
After each player guess: Apply rules R1–R8 to update these lists
Detect signals: Check each coaching signal (S1–S7) against the player's actual guess history
At game end: Generate a debrief that combines the scoring (from main knowledge file) with the deductive coaching signals
Report format: For each turn, show (a) what the player guessed, (b) the response, (c) what could have been deduced, (d) whether the player exploited that deduction in their next guess

guess_history.key_inference: Exactly 2 of {5,6,7,8} are in the secret, none in those positions
Exactly 1 of {1,2,0,9} is in the secret at its position (combined with later guesses → 0 in pos 3)
Confirms via intersection that the shared digit between 1209 and 5209 (which is 2, 0, or 9) is the present one
Three-way intersection of 1209, 5209, 1205 → only 0 is common across all → 0 is present and in position 3
One of {1,9,3,5} present but in wrong position. Need more info.
HARD ELIMINATION: digits 1, 9, 4, 5 are all absent. Now turn 5 collapses: 3 MUST be the present digit from 1935
3 is confirmed present (from turn 6 collapse). So one more of {2,8,7} is present. The 1B is 3 in pos 1.
5 absent, 3 present → one of {6,2} is the second present digit. Combined with turn 1 (2 of {6,7,8} present), 6 must be the one. So second digit from turn 7 is 7 or 8.

worked_example_from_real_game.final_deduction: Position 1 = 3, position 3 = 0, position 4 = 6, position 2 = either 7 or 8. Two candidates: 3706 or 3806. Optimal turn 9 guess: either one (3B 0C response identifies the other).
coaching_observations: Turns 2, 3, 4 (1209, 5209, 1205) were excellent — three guesses with overlapping digits forced the position-3=0 deduction by intersection
Turn 6 (1945) was the critical breakthrough — the 0B 0C result collapsed turn 5 into a forced deduction (3 must be present)
Turn 7 (3287) was strong — tested the unknown digits from {6,7,8} while including the now-confirmed 3

Turn 8 (6235) was reasonable in form but late in timing: the 5 acted as neutral filler (per R11 — known-absent digits contribute zero bulls/cows and don't waste information) and 6 + 3 were active probes. The real critique is timing: by this point the player could already have narrowed to a 2-candidate set, so a discriminating probe of 3706 or 3806 directly would have ended the game in 1-2 more turns
Net assessment: solid mid-game (turns 1-7), one wasted move at turn 8
